notes: ESG-first profiles weight ≥0.30 (impact investing); financial-first ≤0.10 (residual screen only). Khan et al. show material ESG issues predict returns; immaterial ones do not.

citation: Novy-Marx (2013) 'The Other Side of Value: The Gross Profitability Premium'; Fama & French (2015) 'A Five-Factor Model'; Asness, Frazzini & Pedersen (2019) 'Quality Minus Junk'
notes: Gross profitability (Novy-Marx) and operating profitability (Fama-French RMW) are among the strongest cross-sectional predictors.

citation: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) 'Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers'; Carhart (1997) 'On Persistence in Mutual Fund Performance'; Amihud (2002) 'Illiquidity and Stock Returns'
notes: Momentum (6-12 month) is a robust factor but excluded from IC evaluation to avoid circularity with return proxy. Weight kept moderate; set to zero in ex-market variant.

citation: Barney (1991) 'Firm Resources and Sustained Competitive Advantage'; Dechow, Ge & Schrand (2010) 'Understanding Earnings Quality'; Fairfield & Yohn (2001) 'Using Asset Turnover and Profit Margin to Forecast Changes in Profitability'

citation: Sharpe (1966) 'Mutual Fund Performance'; Sortino & van der Meer (1991) 'Downside Risk'; Ang et al. (2006) 'The Cross-Section of Volatility and Expected Returns'

citation: Lakonishok, Shleifer & Vishny (1994) 'Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk'; Chan, Karceski & Lakonishok (2003) 'The Level and Persistence of Growth Rates'
notes: Moderate weight reflects mean-reversion tendency of extreme growth. Excludes price momentum to avoid look-ahead bias.

citation: Fama & French (1992) 'The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns'; Fama & French (1993) 'Common Risk Factors'; Asness et al. (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere'
notes: Value premium is well-documented but has weakened post-2010. Low-to-moderate weight balances value trap risk.

citation: Bhojraj & Lee (2002) 'Who Is My Peer? A Valuation-Based Approach'; Daniel & Titman (1997) 'Evidence on the Characteristics of Cross Sectional Variation in Stock Returns'
